title: The idea from the bath
setting: Monday afternoon at the office. On Friday, Tanaka-san asked Yuki for an idea for the next campaign, and he wants it today. Her coworker and friend Mai (Kimura-san at work) sits at the next desk.

speakers.name: Tanaka-san
speakers.voice: male, 40s, calm and kind, polite office speech

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: yuki-san, sengetsu no kyanpeen, kekka ga demashita yo. amari yokunakatta desu ne.
lines.ja: ユキさん、先月のキャンペーン、結果が出ましたよ。あまり良くなかったですね。
lines.kana: ゆきさん、せんげつのきゃんぺーん、けっかがでましたよ。あまりよくなかったですね。
lines.english: Yuki-san, last month's campaign results are in. I'm afraid they weren't very good.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。今度こそ、結果を出したいですね。
lines.kana: そうですか。こんどこそ、けっかをだしたいですね。
lines.english: I see. This time I really want to get results.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: kin'youbi ni tanonda aidea, kyoujuu ni onegai shimasu ne. ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara.
lines.ja: 金曜日に頼んだアイデア、今日中にお願いしますね。いいアイデアなら、すぐハンコを押しますから。
lines.kana: きんようびにたのんだあいであ、きょうじゅうにおねがいしますね。いいあいであなら、すぐはんこをおしますから。
lines.english: The idea I asked you for on Friday: I'd like it by the end of today. If it's a good one, I'll put my stamp on it straight away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mai, chotto soudan ga aru n da kedo. asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru noni, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai no.
lines.ja: マイ、ちょっと相談があるんだけど。朝からずっと頭使ってるのに、全然いいアイデアが浮かばないの。
lines.kana: まい、ちょっとそうだんがあるんだけど。あさからずっとあたまつかってるのに、ぜんぜんいいあいであがうかばないの。
lines.english: Mai, can I ask your advice? I've been racking my brains all morning, and I can't come up with a single good idea.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: atama tsukaisugi da yo. chotto yasundara?
lines.ja: 頭使いすぎだよ。ちょっと休んだら？
lines.kana: あたまつかいすぎだよ。ちょっとやすんだら？
lines.english: You're thinking too hard. Why not take a little break?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: datte, kinou ofuro de sugoku ii aidea ga ukanda noni, wasurechatta no.
lines.ja: だって、昨日お風呂ですごくいいアイデアが浮かんだのに、忘れちゃったの。
lines.kana: だって、きのうおふろですごくいいあいであがうかんだのに、わすれちゃったの。
lines.english: But last night in the bath, a really good idea came to me, and now I've forgotten it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e, memo toranakatta no? watashi wa, aidea ga ukandara, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru yo.
lines.ja: え、メモ取らなかったの？私は、アイデアが浮かんだら、すぐメモを取るようにしてるよ。
lines.kana: え、めもとらなかったの？わたしは、あいであがうかんだら、すぐめもをとるようにしてるよ。
lines.english: What, you didn't write it down? Whenever an idea comes to me, I make a point of writing it down right away.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: ofuro de memo nanka toreru wake nai jan!
lines.ja: お風呂でメモなんか取れるわけないじゃん！
lines.kana: おふろでめもなんかとれるわけないじゃん！
lines.english: How am I supposed to take notes in the bath?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: a, chotto matte. kinou no yoru, ofuro no ato de denwa kureta yo ne?
lines.ja: あ、ちょっと待って。昨日の夜、お風呂のあとで電話くれたよね？
lines.kana: あ、ちょっとまって。きのうのよる、おふろのあとででんわくれたよね？
lines.english: Oh, hang on. Last night, you called me after your bath, didn't you?

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, sou datta? tsukaretete, zenzen oboetenai.
lines.ja: え、そうだった？疲れてて、全然覚えてない。
lines.kana: え、そうだった？つかれてて、ぜんぜんおぼえてない。
lines.english: Huh, did I? I was so tired, I don't remember at all.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: sugoi aidea ukanda! tte itteta kara, ichiou memo totta no. hora.
lines.ja: 「すごいアイデア浮かんだ！」って言ってたから、一応メモ取ったの。ほら。
lines.kana: 「すごいあいであうかんだ！」っていってたから、いちおうめもとったの。ほら。
lines.english: You said, "I've had an amazing idea!" so I wrote it down, just in case. Look.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: etto, atarashii aji no namae o, okyakusan ni kimete morau kyanpeen. sou sou, kore!
lines.ja: えっと、新しい味の名前を、お客さんに決めてもらうキャンペーン。そうそう、これ！
lines.kana: えっと、あたらしいあじのなまえを、おきゃくさんにきめてもらうきゃんぺーん。そうそう、これ！
lines.english: Let's see: "A campaign where customers choose the name of the new flavour." Yes, yes, this is it!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: kore nara, kitto tanaka-san mo hanko oshite kureru shi, kekka mo daseru yo.
lines.ja: これなら、きっと田中さんもハンコ押してくれるし、結果も出せるよ。
lines.kana: これなら、きっとたなかさんもはんこおしてくれるし、けっかもだせるよ。
lines.english: With this, I bet Tanaka-san will give it his stamp, and we'll get results too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: 田中さん、アイデア持ってきました！
lines.kana: たなかさん、あいであもってきました！
lines.english: Tanaka-san, I've brought you my idea!

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.
lines.ja: 面白いですね、これ。じゃあ、ハンコを押しますね。
lines.kana: おもしろいですね、これ。じゃあ、はんこをおしますね。
lines.english: This is interesting. All right, I'll put my stamp on it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: arigatou gozaimasu! jitsu wa, kimura-san ga memo o totte kureta n desu.
lines.ja: ありがとうございます！実は、木村さんがメモを取ってくれたんです。
lines.kana: ありがとうございます！じつは、きむらさんがめもをとってくれたんです。
lines.english: Thank you! Actually, Kimura-san wrote it down for me.

lines.speaker: tanaka
lines.romaji: sou desu ka. futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne.
lines.ja: そうですか。二人で、今度こそ結果を出してくださいね。
lines.kana: そうですか。ふたりで、こんどこそけっかをだしてくださいね。
lines.english: I see. Then the two of you, make sure you get results this time.

questions.english: What happened with Yuki's campaign idea?

choices.english: Yuki couldn't come up with anything, so Mai gave Tanaka-san one of her own ideas, and he approved it.
Yuki forgot the idea she had in the bath, but Mai had written it down when Yuki phoned her, and Tanaka-san approved it.
Yuki remembered her bath idea after a short break, but Tanaka-san said it needed more work before he'd stamp it.

questions.explanation: Line 3: Tanaka-san wants Yuki's campaign idea by the end of the day. Line 6: a great idea came to Yuki in the bath last night, but she has forgotten it. Lines 9-11: she phoned Mai after her bath, and Mai wrote the idea down just in case. Line 15: Tanaka-san likes it and presses his hanko on it, which means he approves. A is wrong: the idea was Yuki's own. Mai only wrote it down, and Yuki tells Tanaka-san so (line 16). C is wrong: Yuki never remembers it by herself. She reads it in Mai's notes (line 12), and Tanaka-san approves it on the spot.

questions.english: At lunch, Mai hands you her phone with a game on it and says, "kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?" You play a round. Tell her it really makes you think.
questions.ja: これ、最近ハマってるゲーム。やってみる？
questions.kana: これ、さいきんはまってるげーむ。やってみる？
questions.romaji: kore, saikin hamatteru geemu. yatte miru?
questions.answer: Say the game makes you think with atama o tsukau, casually atama tsukau, with kekkou or metcha for 'really': kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.

modelAnswers.romaji: kono geemu, kekkou atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: このゲーム、結構頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: This game really makes you think.

modelAnswers.romaji: muzukashii! kore, metcha atama tsukau ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 難しい！これ、めっちゃ頭使うね。
modelAnswers.english: It's hard! This really gets your brain working.

questions.explanation: Yuki has been racking her brains since the morning (line 4, asa kara zutto atama tsukatteru), and Mai tells her she's overdoing it (line 5, atama tsukaisugi da yo). A game or a job that makes you think is one that 'uses your head': atama o tsukau, in casual speech usually without o. Don't mix it up with atama ga ii (be clever), or with ki o tsukau, which means being considerate. With a friend, casual is right.

questions.english: At the end, Tanaka-san tells Yuki and Mai what he wants from them this time. What did he say?
questions.ja: 田中さんは最後に何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんはさいごになんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa saigo ni nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: This time, make sure you get results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please go and receive the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o moratte kudasai ne

choices.english: This time, please take the results.
choices.romaji: kondo koso kekka o totte kudasai ne

questions.explanation: Line 17: 'futari de, kondo koso kekka o dashite kudasai ne'. Yuki used it in line 2 (kondo koso, kekka o dashitai desu ne), and Mai in line 13 (kekka mo daseru yo). Results you achieve are something you put out yourself: kekka o dasu. In line 1 Tanaka-san used the other verb, kekka ga demashita. There the results came out by themselves, meaning they were announced. B is wrong: morau means being handed something, so kekka o morau only fits getting a results sheet. C is wrong: toru works in ten o toru (get a score) and memo o toru, but results aren't 'taken'. You deliver them with dasu.

questions.english: Tanaka-san comes to your desk and says, "raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne." Ask him to wait a moment while you write it down.
questions.ja: 来週の会議、時間が変わったので、今言いますね。
questions.kana: らいしゅうのかいぎ、じかんがかわったので、いまいいますね。
questions.romaji: raishuu no kaigi, jikan ga kawatta node, ima iimasu ne.
questions.answer: Ask him to wait while you take a note, with memo o toru in polite form: chotto matte kudasai, memo o torimasu. He's your manager, so stay polite.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, chotto matte kudasai. ima memo o torimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、ちょっと待ってください。今メモを取ります。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, just a moment, please. I'll write it down.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, memo o torimasu node, chotto matte kudasai.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、メモを取りますので、ちょっと待ってください。
modelAnswers.english: Sorry, let me take a note. Just a moment, please.

questions.explanation: Mai makes a point of noting ideas down the moment they come (line 7, sugu memo o toru you ni shiteru), and she wrote Yuki's idea down during the call (line 11, ichiou memo totta). Yuki tells Tanaka-san that Kimura-san took it down for her (line 16, memo o totte kureta). As in English, you 'take' notes: memo o toru. Memo suru means the same and is just as common. A note you leave for someone is memo o nokosu. With your manager, use torimasu and matte kudasai.

questions.english: Mai says everyone wants to get Tanaka-san something for his birthday, and asks you, "nee, nani ga ii to omou?" You've thought about it, but nothing comes to mind. Tell her.
questions.ja: 田中さんの誕生日、みんなで何かあげようって。ねえ、何がいいと思う？
questions.kana: たなかさんのたんじょうび、みんなでなにかあげようって。ねえ、なにがいいとおもう？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san no tanjoubi, minna de nanika ageyou tte. nee, nani ga ii to omou?
questions.answer: Say no good idea comes to mind with aidea ga ukabu in the negative: zenzen ii aidea ukabanai. With Mai, casual is right.

modelAnswers.ja: うーん、全然いいアイデア浮かばない。
modelAnswers.english: Hmm, I can't come up with any good ideas at all.

modelAnswers.romaji: nan darou. mada ii aidea ga ukabanai n da yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: 何だろう。まだいいアイデアが浮かばないんだよね。
modelAnswers.english: Good question. No good idea has come to me yet.

questions.explanation: Yuki complains that no good idea comes to her (line 4, zenzen ii aidea ga ukabanai), though a great one came to her in the bath (line 6, ukanda). Ideas float up into your mind on their own, so the idea is the subject with ga: aidea ga ukabu, and casual speech often drops the ga. It is mostly heard in the negative, like this. Ukabu reports an idea coming, or not coming, to mind, as in sugoi aidea ukanda! (line 11). To offer an idea, 'I've got an idea!', people say ii kangae ga aru! or omoitsuita! With Mai, casual is right.

questions.english: Yuki brings her idea to Tanaka-san. What did he do?
questions.ja: 田中さんは、ユキのアイデアをどうしましたか？
questions.kana: たなかさんは、ゆきのあいであをどうしましたか？
questions.romaji: tanaka-san wa, yuki no aidea o dou shimashita ka?

choices.english: He asked Yuki to put her own seal on it first, before he read it.
He gave it a fun 'good job' stamp, like a teacher, but hasn't decided yet.
He approved it: his seal on the plan means it can go ahead.

questions.explanation: Line 15: 'omoshiroi desu ne, kore. jaa, hanko o oshimasu ne.' In a Japanese office a manager approves a plan by pressing his personal seal (hanko) on it, so this means 'yes, go ahead'. He promised it in line 3 (ii aidea nara, sugu hanko o oshimasu kara), and Mai predicted it in line 13. A is wrong: nobody asks Yuki for her own seal. B is wrong: a fun rubber stamp, like a teacher's 'well done', is a sutanpu. A hanko is a personal seal, and you press it: hanko o osu.
